- When sentiment is high (≥0.6) and forecast shows strong upward bias, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid over-optimism.  
- When sentiment is low (≤0.3) and forecast shows strong downward bias, increase forecast by 5–10% to avoid pessimism.  
- If forecast spikes sharply after a recent low, reduce the spike by 10–20% to account for mean reversion.  
- If forecast consistently overestimates mid-range values (e.g., 65–67) while true values are lower, apply a 3–5% downward adjustment for 3–5 day horizon.  
- If sentiment is volatile (rapid swings) and forecast is smooth, introduce a 1–2% lag correction to align with sentiment momentum.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is consistently below forecast, apply a 2–5% downward bias correction for the next 7–14 days.  
- If sentiment is rising and forecast is flat, add a 2–3% upward adjustment to reflect sentiment momentum.
